title: 40 Economic impact of selling goat kids at weaning or after an extended feeding period
content:
Abstract
Goat meat is a vital animal protein in many societies around the world and is growing in popularity in the United States. However, there remains a need for optimized production strategies of meat goats in the U.S. to support the sustainability of this expanding industry. Texas remains the leading goat state in the U.S., and in this region commercial producers traditionally market their goats between 60 and 180 days of age through a regional livestock auction where prices can fluctuate depending on season, goat body weight and fleshing ability. In this study, we investigated goat growth and corresponding market values to better understand the influences on meat goat prices in this setting. At the Texas A&M AgriLife Center in San Angelo the objective was to evaluate the cost of gain and feed efficiency of meat goats divided into three groups by weaning weight (n = 50 per group); “smaller (SM)” (13.6–20.4 kg), “moderate (MD)” (20.5–27.2 kg), and “larger (LG)” (27.3–34 kg. Boer X Spanish crossbred goats were placed in drylot pens by group and provided ad libitum access to a total-mixed ration (~18% protein). Goat weights were recorded at weaning (~12 weeks) and at biweekly intervals throughout the trial. At the conclusion of the feeding period, wether goats were marketed at a major regional auction in San Angelo, Texas to determine goat values after feeding. During the feeding period, MD goats exhibited the highest average daily gain (ADG) compared to LG goats (p< 0.001), while LG goats outperformed SM goats (p< 0.001). MD goats achieved the highest ADG during the second and fourth weigh periods, whereas LG goats led in the third weigh period. The net value of goats, calculated as gross value minus feed cost, provided key insights for producers. MD goats achieved a higher net value by Day 56 compared to their initial value at Day 0 in early June. Conversely, LG and SM goats had a higher net value at weaning than after 56 days on feed. The superior ADG of MD goats suggests they had the greatest growth among the classifications. Market prices in 2024 matched a 5-year average, which provided valuable guidance for producers wanting to increase profits from their herds. By connecting goat weight, feed efficiency, and market value, this research offers insight into meat goat growth patterns and insights on market factors affecting their commercial value. These results also offer practical strategies that can enhance decision-making for meat goat production. This study emphasizes the importance of aligning livestock management with market demands. The findings also highlight the potential for predictive modeling to optimize profitability, enabling researchers to explore broader applications in livestock production systems, such as precision agriculture and supply chain management.
